Well so before you go too far lets get down to the key details here. look how i have this one face clicked, and i see the whole uv outlined from the one face [Image #87] ok so im going to click a new face, and look. the uv is the same outlined shape. doesnt care what face im clicking on from the base cube. its all the same thing. [Image #88] 

you might be asking yourself well thats dumb how do they paint each face then? well the difference is that i click on texture create and when i do that this is what happens in blockbench [Image #89] 

you are confusing two different steps here, the uv mesh is not the same as the texture mesh that comes from it
resolution: The UV-layout slice, with a key conceptual correction from the user: the UV MESH is NOT the texture. (1) The UV mesh (the mapping the UV editor shows): a base cube maps EVERY face to the FULL unit square — clicking any face shows the whole 16x16 outline because every face samples the entire texture. New fullFaceUV(m) in editMesh.ts (each face's own projection normalized to fill [0,1]^2) is now the default; cuboid()/cylinder() call it. (2) The texture (the box-net colored regions, Blockbench image 89): a downstream artifact created by 'create texture' that packs faces into atlas regions AND remaps their UVs — that is unwrap() (the box-net packer, kept) and is Phase 5c, not the default. So req_1002 (box-net) and req_1003 (fill the square) were both this confusion and now belong to 5c; the panel's button became 'Reset UV' (fullFaceUV) instead of Unwrap. editMesh 25/25 (the fresh-cuboid test now asserts every face fills the full unit square; the box-net contiguity test now calls unwrap() explicitly). Hot-reload TSX, nothing committed.
